description.narrative:
This project proposes the establishment of a Community Soil Care Clinic to support farmers in South Lebanon whose lands were affected by the 2024 Israeli aggression. The clinic will help farmers test their soils for heavy metal contamination, assess biological activity, and receive customized guidance on soil regeneration using bioremediation techniques such as compost, biochar, and phytoremediation. By offering accessible, science-based soil diagnostics and advice, the clinic will relieve farmers of thehigh costs of commercial soil testing and contribute to restoring their agricultural livelihoods. The clinic will be hosted at Al Safir Farms in Ghaziyeh - Saida, a partner farm equipped with a composting unit and learning center. A mobile clinic team will conduct soil sampling in affected agricultural areas and perform on-site testing for heavy metals using a handheld XRF analyzer. Based on test results (including contamination levels, soil biology, and pH) the team will provide farmers with tailored recommendations for soil remediation and regeneration. Through this initiative, the Community Soil Care Clinic will serve as a hub for soil restoration and farmer education, promoting environmental recovery and agricultural resilience in post-conflict SouthLebanon.
The project purpose is to build the capacities of the local communities in developing, field-testing and documenting bioremediation methodologies adapted to local conditions in contaminated agricultural lands in the south of Lebanon. In the long term, the aim is to contribute to the agricultural land rehabilitation, ensure the production of safe crops, and support farmers affected by the war in restoring their livelihoods.

participating-org.narrative: The Bioremediation Coalition in Lebanon is a knowledge-sharing working group established in October 2024, in response to the environmental impacts caused by the Israeli aggression. The coalition is coordinated by SOILS Permaculture Association Lebanon and brings together activists and agroecology practitioners from across the country, along with two international bioremediation consultants from the U.S. and Canada. The coalition was formed to collaborate on rehabilitating agricultural land affected by the conflict throughthe use of bioremediation techniques, aiming to reduce soil contamination, minimize health risks to farmers and consumers, and support the restoration of agricultural livelihoods.Its members bring complementary expertise in agroecology, permaculture, composting, bioremediation, project management, landscape design, and environmental research. Over the past year, the group has been meeting regularly on a monthly basis, engaging with local stakeholders to assess ongoing efforts in soil regeneration and identify gaps and needs in bioremediation practices.
